name: Making sense of video
gist: Helping models understand what happens over time in videos, track changes, and answer questions about video content without watching every single frame.
explain: A video is a sequence of images played in quick succession. To understand it, a model needs to grasp not just what is in each individual frame but what is changing, what is moving, and how events unfold over time. You could theoretically process every single frame independently, but that is wasteful and misses the point — video is fundamentally about change. A person walking across a room is the same person in frame one and frame two, but their position changed. A ball falling shows acceleration. A scene getting darker might mean the sun is setting or a shadow is crossing. Understanding video means building a representation of temporal flow, causality, and continuity, not just a stack of static pictures.

The hardness comes from multiple angles. First, videos are huge. A minute of video at 30 frames per second is 1,800 frames. Processing all of them with a heavy image encoder is computationally expensive. Second, you need to figure out what matters. If a camera is fixed on an empty parking lot for an hour with one car parking for five minutes, the important information is 'a car arrived,' not 'most of the lot was empty.' Models need to learn to focus on significant events. Third, some understanding requires longer-term reasoning. If you watch a movie scene, you need to remember who characters are from earlier in the film, understand plot threads, track relationships. Finally, questions about video require different reasoning: action recognition asks 'what is happening?', object tracking asks 'where is that specific thing?' (and it should stay the same thing across frames), video captioning asks 'describe this event in words,' and video question answering asks 'answer this question about the video content.'

Researchers are building video models that capture temporal structure efficiently. Some use frame sampling — instead of processing every frame, process every fifth or tenth frame, or use a model that learns which frames are most important. Others build models that track motion and flow — computing how pixels move between frames — which lets the model understand not just how things look but how they are moving. Tracking motion this way uses far less computation than processing every pixel in every frame, so it's more efficient. Some use three-dimensional convolutions, treating video like a three-dimensional grid (width, height, time) and letting the model learn patterns that span time. Others compress temporal information early, building a compact summary of 'what happened' before processing details. For action recognition, some models track skeletons or optical flow (the apparent motion of pixels) rather than working with raw video. For object tracking, the model needs to maintain an identity across frames — 'that is the same person even though their angle changed.' The common thread is that all these approaches are trying to make video understanding efficient while preserving the temporal and causal information that makes video different from just a pile of images.

papers.title: FOCUS: Efficient Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Selects less than 2% of video frames while improving accuracy by 11.9% on LongVideoBench for videos longer than 20 minutes.

papers.title: Foresee-to-Ground: From Predictive Temporal Perception to Evidence-Driven Reasoning for Video Temporal Grounding
papers.contribution: Consistently improves grounding accuracy across diverse benchmarks, transfers robustly across VLM backbones, and preserves general video understanding.

papers.title: Fostering Video Reasoning via Next-Event Prediction
papers.contribution: NEP enables scalable training for temporal reasoning, validated on V1-33K dataset with the FutureBench evaluation showing improved coherence in predicting unseen future events.

papers.title: MMDuet2: Enhancing Proactive Interaction of Video MLLMs with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: MMDuet2 outperforms baseline proactive Video MLLMs in response timing and quality on the ProactiveVideoQA benchmark.

papers.title: PhoStream: Benchmarking Real-World Streaming for Omnimodal Assistants in Mobile Scenarios
papers.contribution: Reveals temporal asymmetry where models excel on instant/backward tasks but sharply drop on forward tasks due to responding before required visual-audio cues appear.

papers.title: VideoLoom: A Video Large Language Model for Joint Spatial-Temporal Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on spatial and temporal benchmarks with a novel metric for comprehensive evaluation.

papers.title: VideoMind: A Chain-of-LoRA Agent for Temporal-Grounded Video Reasoning
papers.contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness across 15 benchmarks on grounded VideoQA, video temporal grounding, and general VideoQA tasks.

papers.title: VideoTrace-R1: Long Video-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on long-video benchmarks with largest gains on out-of-domain tasks (Video-Holmes, CG-Bench-Reasoning, VRBench).

papers.title: 4DPC$^2$hat: Towards Dynamic Point Cloud Understanding with Failure-Aware Bootstrapping
papers.contribution: First MLLM for dynamic point clouds with 44K sequences and 200K QA pairs; significantly improves action understanding and temporal reasoning.

papers.title: A Training-Free Framework for Long Video Understanding via Video-Query-Options Similarity
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 5 mainstream benchmarks through training-free approach on LLaVA-Video and Qwen2.5-VL with significant computational efficiency improvements.

papers.title: A.I.R.: Enabling Adaptive, Iterative, and Reasoning-based Frame Selection For Video Question Answering
papers.contribution: A.I.R. outperforms existing frame selection methods, boosts VLM performance, and achieves substantial computational efficiency gains.

papers.title: AD-MIR: Bridging the Gap from Perception to Persuasion in Advertising Video Understanding via Structured Reasoning
papers.contribution: AD-MIR achieves state-of-the-art on AdsQA, surpassing DVD by 1.8 and 9.5 percentage points in strict and relaxed accuracy.

papers.title: Decomposed Attention Fusion in MLLMs for Training-free Video Reasoning Segmentation
papers.contribution: Achieves performance comparable to training-based methods on referring and reasoning VOS benchmarks using purely training-free approach.

papers.title: Divid: Disentangled Spatial-Temporal Modeling within LLMs for Temporally Grounded Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Divid improves temporal alignment accuracy while minimizing redundant visual processing and enabling better context efficiency.

papers.title: MetaphorVU: Towards Metaphorical Video Understanding
papers.contribution: MetaphorBoost achieves consistent performance improvement and provides insights for advancing MLLMs' metaphorical comprehension capabilities.

papers.title: Progressive Online Video Understanding with Evidence-Aligned Timing and Transparent Decisions
papers.contribution: Thinking-QwenVL improves accuracy on StreamingBench from 67.63% to 71.60%, enabling precise response timing aligned with visual evidence.

papers.title: QueryStream: Advancing Streaming Video Understanding with Query-Aware Pruning and Proactive Response
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on StreamingBench and OVO-Bench while pruning over 70% of visual tokens, generalizing to offline context-denoising.

papers.title: StreamingVLM: Real-Time Understanding for Infinite Video Streams
papers.contribution: Achieves 66.18% win rate against GPT-4O mini on Inf-Streams-Eval benchmark with 2-hour videos, maintaining 8 FPS real-time performance on single H100.

papers.title: Task-Aware Mechanism: Hybrid MoE Vision Tower Towards Holistic Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves SOTA performance among models with comparable LLMs on most video benchmarks and remains competitive against stronger-LLM baselines.

papers.title: Towards One-to-Many Temporal Grounding
papers.contribution: The model achieves state-of-the-art EtF1 of 43.65% on OMTG Bench, outperforming Gemini 2.5 Pro and Seed-1.8 by 15.85% and 15.61%.

papers.title: TripleSumm: Adaptive Triple-Modality Fusion for Video Summarization
papers.contribution: TripleSumm achieves state-of-the-art performance by a large margin on four video summarization benchmarks including the newly introduced MoSu.

papers.title: VidBridge-R1: Bridging QA and Captioning for RL-based Video Understanding Models with Intermediate Proxy Tasks
papers.contribution: First versatile video reasoning model achieving significant performance gains on both QA and captioning within one model.

papers.title: Video-BCI: Bayesian Cognitive Integration of Self-Prior Hypotheses for Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results across six benchmarks, improving MMVU by 3.8% through enhanced reasoning and bias mitigation.

papers.title: VideoBrain: Learning Adaptive Frame Sampling for Long Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves 3.5-9.0% improvement over baseline while using 30-40% fewer frames with strong cross-dataset generalization to short videos.

papers.title: VideoJudge: Bootstrapping Enables Scalable Supervision of MLLM-as-a-Judge for Video Understanding
papers.contribution: VideoJudge-7B outperforms larger MLLM judges like Qwen2.5-VL-32B and Qwen2.5-VL-72B, demonstrating video inputs are crucial for video understanding task evaluation.

papers.title: VideoNSA: Native Sparse Attention Scales Video Understanding
papers.contribution: Reliably scales to 128K tokens with improved long-video understanding, temporal reasoning, and spatial performance over token-compression baselines.
